title: Himiko
summary: Himiko was a 3rd-century CE shaman-queen of Yamatai in ancient Japan, documented in the Chinese Records of the Three Kingdoms. Chosen to restore peace following decades of internal warfare, she ruled through spiritual authority from a secluded fortress, established tributary diplomatic relations with the Chinese Wei dynasty in 238 CE, and was entombed beneath a massive burial mound upon her death.

uncertainty.note: Birth estimated c. 175–183 CE; Chinese Wei chronicles place her death around 247–248 CE.

where.modern_name: Sakurai, Nara Prefecture, Japan (Hashihaka Kofun, one candidate for her tomb; Yamatai's location, northern Kyushu or Yamato, is debated)
where.historical_name: Yamatai (associated with Hashihaka Kofun), ancient Wa (Japan)

importance.justification: First recorded sovereign of ancient Japan in contemporary foreign dynastic annals, linking early Wa culture to continental diplomacy.

sources.title: Himiko (fl. 3rd c.)
sources.publisher: Encyclopedia.com (Women in World History: A Biographical Encyclopedia)
sources.author: Linda L. Johnson

reviewer_note: Least sure of the geographical location of Yamatai, debated between northern Kyushu and the Kinai/Nara region (anchored here to Hashihaka Kofun in Nara).
